_about: ILLUSTRATIVE JURISDICTIONS, NOT AUTHORITATIVE ADMINISTRATIVE BOUNDARIES. These are coarse bounding boxes standing in for the real polygons while an authoritative boundary file is unavailable. They exist so alert routing has somewhere to route to. A deployment must replace them with the actual jurisdiction geometry published by the state, because an alert delivered to the wrong body is worse than one that was never sent: it creates a record of notification without anyone able to act on it.
_coordinate_order: [longitude, latitude], WGS84, matching GeoJSON and PostGIS
_escalation_tier: Lowest tier containing the hotspot is notified first, so a municipal body is reached before a state board rather than both being alerted and each assuming the other is handling it.
_contact: Addresses are deliberately on the reserved .invalid domain. No real inbox is contacted by a seeded deployment.

authorities.name: East Delhi Municipal Zone
authorities.note: Covers Anand Vihar, Vivek Vihar and the Ghazipur landfill, which is where the detector finds the largest and most persistent excesses.

authorities.name: West Delhi Municipal Zone
authorities.note: Covers Punjabi Bagh, Wazirpur and the Mundka industrial belt.

authorities.name: South Delhi Municipal Zone
authorities.note: Covers R K Puram, Okhla and the Okhla waste-to-energy plant.

authorities.name: North Delhi Municipal Zone
authorities.note: Covers Bawana, Narela and the Jahangirpuri corridor.

authorities.name: Delhi Pollution Control Committee
authorities.note: State board covering the whole NCT. Overlaps every municipal zone deliberately: it is the fallback for ground no zone claims, and the escalation tier keeps it from being alerted alongside a zone for the same event.

authorities.name: Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board, Kanpur
authorities.note: The second pilot node. Present so a hotspot detected outside Delhi routes to a real body rather than counting as unrouted.

authorities.name: Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, Coimbatore
authorities.note: The data-poor southern node. It has no usable PM2.5 monitoring, so this jurisdiction will route nothing until a sensor tier exists there -- which is precisely the gap the project is about.
